title: Building Trust in an AI SRE Agent: Royal Caribbean and LiveRamp at AWS re:Invent by PagerDuty
summary: How do you trust an AI agent with incident response? LiveRamp and Royal Caribbean share their approach to PagerDuty’s AI SRE agent at AWS re:Invent.
body_markdown:
An alert fires at 3 a.m. The on-call engineer wakes up, opens their laptop, and spends the next 20 minutes triaging and diagnosing what’s broken. Critical context is scattered across dashboards, runbooks, and the memories of other responders, and the conversation about how to fix it is split across just as many channels.


The lost time is more than frustrating. It slows resolution and hurts the business.


##### SRE agents help streamline response from detection to remediation to prevention


[Paige](https://www.pagerduty.com/platform/ai-agents/sre/) , PagerDuty’s SRE agent, can start investigating the moment an alert fires, before anyone gets the late-night nudge. Teams can also set it up to work side by side with the responder, with a human in the loop. The agent surfaces critical context the responder needs, recommends a workflow, and can drive the response all the way through remediation.


Every incident also makes the next one easier. Paige keeps a shared memory of what happened, what worked, and who was involved. Over time, that turns tribal knowledge into organizational intelligence, helping teams prevent repeat incidents and moving them closer to autonomous operations.


But handing incident response to an AI agent raises an important question: How much do you trust it?


Royal Caribbean and LiveRamp are answering that question step by step, starting with where agents fit and where humans stay in charge.


##### Royal Caribbean: Mapping the journey toward AI-enabled autonomous operations


Alice McElroy, Director, IT Infrastructure and Operations for


[Royal Caribbean](https://www.royalcaribbean.com/) , sees a path from reactive to proactive, then to preventive and predictive incident management, with zero-touch operations as a long-term vision. Today, her team uses AI in an advisory role, and she recognizes that getting further will take a trust-building journey.


The team started by assessing top pain points, including aspects of triage, and discussed how SRE agents could help alleviate the burden. They also shared their concerns about relying on AI and what it would take to build their trust.


##### LiveRamp: Planning for AI-powered incident management


Triage was also a time-consuming challenge for


[LiveRamp](https://liveramp.com/) ’s Samrat Ghosh, Staff Technical Lead Manager, Quality Engineering & Incident Management. His team looked to Paige to reduce


[MTTR](https://www.pagerduty.com/resources/devops/learn/what-is-mttr/) and engineer burnout.


The team saw the value, and they knew the rollout would take careful planning. That meant choosing pilot use cases, setting approval gates and guardrails, and integrating Paige with their existing runbooks, tools, and escalation policies.


“A 3 a.m. page used to mean opening half a dozen tabs and spending 20 minutes piecing together what broke. With Paige, a structured diagnosis is waiting before we’ve even opened our laptops. Our engineers still make the call, but now they start with answers instead of questions.”


##### Get customer insights at AWS re:Invent


McElroy and Ghosh will share what they’ve learned, from building trust in an AI agent to the lessons that made the difference, at AWS re:Invent.


Join us at the Wynn on Tuesday, Dec. 1, at 4 p.m. to hear from Royal Caribbean and LiveRamp. Add the session “


[3 a.m. and Already Fixed: How PagerDuty’s SRE Agent Is Rewriting Incident Response](https://info.pagerduty.com/PagerDutyAWSreInvent2026.html) ” to your calendar now.
